title: Managed Identity vs Service Principals
description: Compare managed identities and service principals to decide which identity model fits your Azure application.

data.text: Two Ways to Authenticate Azure Resources
Both managed identities and service principals are identities in Entra ID, but they solve different problems. Service principals require you to manage credentials. Managed identities do not.

cards.title: Managed Identity
cards.description: Azure-managed identity with no secrets to store or rotate.

cards.title: Service Principal
cards.description: App registration-based identity with client credentials.
pros: Full control over certificates and secrets
cons: You must protect the client secret or certificate
Secrets expire and must be rotated

rows: You manage client secrets or certificates

data.title: Recommendation
data.text: Use managed identities for code running in Azure. Use service principals only when you need to run outside Azure, such as in GitHub Actions or local development.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identities are simpler and more secure for Azure-native workloads.
Service principals are necessary for non-Azure environments.
You can use both: a service principal for local dev and managed identity in production.
